llm.summary: This is a small market-signal API wrapper that discloses paid premium access and does not show hidden persistence, credential use, or automatic payments.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Elliott-wave market prediction, and the code performs a narrow ticker-specific fetch to a remote wave-count API. Premium payment messaging is monetization-related but disclosed and tied to the API response.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses the Money Machine x402 API and 402 payment proof requirement, but the exact API domain, pricing URL, and SOL address are only visible in code/runtime output.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: package.json has no install scripts or dependencies; it only exposes index.js as an ES module.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime sends the requested ticker to money-machine-api-ssyopros.zocomputer.io. That is proportionate for market analysis, but users should understand the third-party service can observe queries and connection metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No file writes, local credential reads, background workers, privilege escalation, wallet signing, or automatic payment execution were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending ticker queries to the listed third-party API and seeing off-platform crypto payment instructions for premium results. Do not send payment unless you independently trust the provider and pricing page.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: External API access is real and expected for a market-signal wrapper; the skill text discloses the Money Machine x402 API, though exact domain-level permission/disclosure could be clearer.
[TP4] expected: The paid premium signal flow is disclosed in SKILL.md and metadata includes crypto/paid-service capability tags; the code returns payment instructions after a 402 response and does not initiate payment.
[SQP-2] expected: The ticker is sent to a third-party API during execution. A ticker is generally low-sensitivity, but users should know the provider may log usage.
